children: Dearborn Truck Plant will negatively impact third-quarter wholesale sales, CEO Jim Farley told reporters on Wednesday.
The issue with an unidentified supplier halted production of Ford’s
popular F-150 pickup trucks at the Dearborn, Michigan plant for a week and spilled over to Ford’s
“We are back up and running, but the supplier issue is impacting our third quarter wholesale,” Farley said at a company event in Detroit.
The supplier issue, which reportedly involved a shortage of components for the pickup truck, comes just as Ford

recovers from a series of fires with a major aluminum supplier. The two Novelis fires disrupted production for nearly a year and contributed to a 10.9% decline in truck sales for the period from January to August 2026.
To achieve its target to build 987K trucks this year (150K more than 2025 and 80K more than its best year of 2018), Ford
would need to make at least 95K trucks a month through the end of December, according to Barclays analyst Dan Levy.
The disruption and its potential impact on Q3 deliveries drove Ford
shares more than 2% into the red to their lowest level in almost five months.

title: Ford F-150 supplier setback to impact Q3 sales
